analysis:
Examined the reconnect-lifecycle change: runLoop now uses an injectable CoordinatorReconnectPolicy (CoordinatorClient.swift:120-141) with a per-attempt CoordinatorSessionRecorder (CoordinatorClientState.swift:509-536) that records open duration and the coordinator's WebSocket close code. Delay is computed via policy.nextDelayRange(after: end), replacing ExponentialBackoff(1,30). The policy type itself is not in the supplied evidence, so its delay bounds (min/max, handling of close codes such as 1012, jitter, and reset) are an unverified contract. A policy that permits very short or zero delays could cause a reconnect storm against the coordinator, which is an availability concern for TB-002. A policy that sets very long delays could cause provider unavailability, which is an availability concern for T-057/A-018. Neither can be concluded without the policy source.

Security-relevant behavior is unchanged. Close-code parsing in sentCloseCode (Connection.swift:492-501) is bounds-checked (content.count >= 2) and uses startIndex-safe indexing. The close code is only logged and fed to the policy; it is not used for authorization. The coordinator is trusted for hop-by-hop handling, and its close code influencing only the retry delay is acceptable. The log line adds close_code, a small integer with no secrets. The per-session defer teardown is unchanged: it resets the capacity session, fails drain barriers, unbinds the chunk batcher, and clears the App Attest resume nonce. appAttestResumeNonce still uses Sodium randomBytes and is generated per connection. The recorder uses an unfair lock and is @unchecked Sendable; recordCloseCode is called on connectionQueue and end() on the actor, both under the lock, so there are no data races. The wsMeta close handling on error paths only adds recording before the existing throw. The receive path and frame-size cap are unchanged.

Remaining question for integration: confirm CoordinatorReconnectPolicy enforces a nonzero minimum delay and a bounded maximum, and that it resets only after sufficiently long sessions, so a malicious or misconfigured coordinator cannot induce tight reconnect loops.
